headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; n8n’s server-side execution plus Kestra’s broad filesystem/network access make the pair unsafe by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and process workflow inputs, while n8n can run AI Agent workflows and server-side nodes. If n8n passes Kestra-produced files or messages into an agent prompt, attacker-controlled content can steer instructions. The pathway is plausible in default orchestration, though not proven as a direct bridge.
conditions: IF n8n workflow inputs include Kestra-generated files or messages without sanitization
IF an n8n AI Agent node treats workflow content as instructions
mitigations: Add a strict content-sanitization step before any AI Agent node
Separate machine-readable data from prompt text in workflow design
Disable automatic ingestion of raw files into prompts
Use allowlisted templates for agent inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Kestra and n8n

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and n8n can process whatever the workflow handles while storing secrets on the server. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, so sensitive data can flow from Kestra into n8n and then out through integrations or model calls. This is a default-dangerous leakage path.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows process logs, database data, or cloud storage data
IF n8n workflows forward those inputs to integrations or AI nodes
mitigations: Restrict both systems to non-sensitive test data
Turn off any AI nodes for workflows handling secrets
Limit n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes
Add redaction before handoff from Kestra to n8n
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and broad network egress; n8n also has write_filesystem and server-side Execute Command/Code nodes. They can both mutate the same server filesystem or connected systems concurrently, and n8n explicitly supports shared state via datastore and connected systems. Without locking, overlapping writes can corrupt jobs or external resources.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or connected system
IF either workflow uses Execute Command or shell tasks concurrently
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and credentials per agent
Serialize writes with a lock or queue
Disable Execute Command where not required
Use idempotent operations for shared resources
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can emit workflow outputs, logs, and notifications, and n8n’s AI Agent node orchestrates tools defined as sub-nodes. If n8n consumes Kestra output as authoritative workflow input, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into downstream actions like emails, API calls, or infrastructure changes. The pair lacks a built-in verification guarantee in the profiles.
conditions: IF n8n uses Kestra outputs as agent context or workflow variables
IF downstream n8n nodes act on those values without validation
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any action node
Require human approval for destructive actions
Compare Kestra outputs against source-of-truth systems
Use schema validation on all handoffs
requires-engineering: add confidence gates for agent-produced facts

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra touches database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and stores secrets per credential on its server. If regulated data is routed through both, retention, residency, or subject-rights handling can diverge across systems. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are routed through both systems
IF retention or deletion settings differ between Kestra and n8n
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between systems
Align retention settings on both platforms
Avoid sending regulated data to workflows that do not need it
Document residency and deletion handling for each integration
requires-engineering: implement policy checks on workflow creation
